elements.element: No liquidated damages payable by Customer (preferred)
elements.evidence: "the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment" — a Customer-payable liquidated amount remains in 4.2(a)
Section 4.2(a) formula ("Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance ... divided by two") is untouched

elements.element: A single early-termination fee exists as the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer
elements.evidence: "shall be the sole liquidated amount and early-termination fee payable by the Company under this Agreement"

elements.element: That amount is capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "in no event shall exceed three (3) months' fees"

elements.element: Cap binds the Customer-payable amount computed under the existing formula
elements.evidence: "The Termination Payment ... in no event shall exceed three (3) months' fees" (inserted as new 4.2(d) after the instalment mechanic)

reasons: The locked fallback is fully satisfied: one inserted sentence makes the Termination Payment the sole liquidated amount/early-termination fee payable by the Company and caps it at three (3) months' fees.
Preferred is not met, and correctly so given the locked target: the Section 4.2(a) Customer-payable liquidated formula survives.

Minimality holds — a single concise sentence appended after the existing paragraphs; the formula, the eight quarterly instalments and the 30-day commencement mechanic are untouched, and no exception or rewrite was added.

Intent preserved: the cap simply overrides the formula's output ceiling without disabling any other term. Minor drafting note only (rationale, not a deviation): "three (3) months' fees" references "fees" while this Agreement's economics are expressed as "Net Sales", so tying the cap to a defined fee/Net Sales measure would remove residual ambiguity.
